entities.name: Carlo Andrea Pozzo di Borgo
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Carlo Andrea Pozzo di Borgo (1764–1842) emerged from the turbulent Corsican political landscape as a fierce opponent of Napoleon Bonaparte, transforming himself into a pivotal Russian diplomat whose influence profoundly shaped European power dynamics in the aftermath of the Napoleonic Wars. Born into a prominent Corsican family in Alata, near Ajaccio, Pozzo di Borgo initially served as procurator-general-syndic of the Corsican Assembly during the French Revolution, aligning with Pasquale Paoli and advocating for Corsican autonomy. His deep-seated rivalry with Bonaparte, stemming from their early political clashes on the island, would become a defining feature of his career, driving him into the service of anti-French coalitions and ultimately, the Russian Empire.

After fleeing Corsica in 1796 following Bonaparte's ascent, Pozzo di Borgo found refuge and opportunity in the courts of various European powers opposed to France. He entered Russian service in 1805, quickly becoming a trusted advisor to Tsar Alexander I. In this capacity, he played a crucial role in orchestrating the coalition against Napoleon, particularly during the critical years leading up to the Congress of Vienna (1814-1815). As Russia's chief plenipotentiary at the Congress, he helped redraw the map of Europe, advocating for a balance of power that would contain French ambitions and secure Russian influence. His subsequent appointment as Russian Ambassador to France (1814-1835) and later to Great Britain (1835-1839) placed him at the heart of European diplomacy for over two decades, where he diligently worked to maintain the Concert of Europe and solidify Russia's standing.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Carlo Andrea Pozzo di Borgo was a crucial figure in shaping post-Napoleonic European diplomacy, particularly through his long tenure as Russian ambassador to France and Great Britain, significantly influencing the Concert of Europe and Russian foreign policy for decades.
